title: ClaimArbitrage positive residual deltas stranded in contract instead of contributing to caller profit
description: In _settleResidualDelta(), when a token has a positive delta (credit in PoolManager), the function calls poolManager.take() to convert the credit to real ERC-20 tokens. These tokens are left in the ClaimArbitrage contract rather than being routed to the caller or converted to profit. Over many executions, value accumulates in the contract requiring manual owner rescue via rescueToken().
impact: Reduces arbitrage profitability for MEV bots, potentially deterring bots from executing claims and slowing yield distribution to Phlimbo stakers. Value systematically leaks from callers to the contract.
attack_path: During execute(), pump/unwind cycle creates positive residual delta
Steps 7-9 only convert reward token to WETH for profit
recommendation: After settling residual deltas, deposit taken tokens back into PoolManager and swap to reward token so they contribute to profit, or sweep non-zero balances to the caller.
